title: Number Theory & Math — Depth Pass
relevance: Medium-High — second wave of CF Div2 C/D number-theory after sieve/GCD/binpow templates; these are the observation + factorization drills that show up in harder OAs and cyan→blue contests.
company_notes: k-th divisor / reconstruct from almost-all divisors (762A / 1165D): O(√n) enumeration and consistency checks. Raise array gcd / share a prime (Enlarge GCD / Bash's Big Day / ABC177E), often as group-compatible IDs. Trailing zeros under multiply-budget ≤m or smallest N with K|N! (Make It Round / ABC280D): Legendre + binary search in quant/OA math. GCD of all aᵢ+x or gcd of pairwise LCMs (Row GCD / Orac and LCM): one-line identity rewrite over brute force.

phases.goal: Spot depth-pass NT where a hidden rewritten invariant replaces an announced sieve/GCD/binpow template.

must_hit.point: After T-primes / Fadi-LCM / Orac-Models, contest NT hides a rewritten invariant: gcd of shifts → gcd of differences; gcd of pairwise LCMs → second-min exponents; floor(n/i) jumps in √n blocks; “make equal in k divides” → total Ω-count.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names at least one of those rewrites (diffs, second-min exponents, floor blocks, or Ω-count) instead of a plain template name.

must_hit.point: Recognize it when constraints are n·√A or A log A feasible, values ≤1e6 invite SPF sieves, or the statement mixes GCD/LCM/divisors with construction, games, or range queries.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites n·√A / A log A feasibility, ≤1e6 SPF, or GCD/LCM mixed with construction/games/range queries.

must_hit.point: OA/interview skins include k-th divisor / reconstruct from almost-all divisors, raise gcd by deleting fewest or sharing a prime, trailing zeros under multiply ≤m / smallest N with K|N!, and GCD of all aᵢ+x or of pairwise LCMs.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps the prompt to one of those four skins from Where it appears.

probes: What rewritten invariant or constraint cue says this is depth-pass NT rather than a plain sieve/GCD/binpow template?
If values are ≤1e6, or you see GCD/LCM mixed with construction/games/queries, what do you reach for?

hints.1: Ask whether the statement hides a rewrite (diffs, second-min exponents, floor blocks, Ω-count) instead of naming a template.
hints.2: Cue triad: n·√A or A log A feasible; values ≤1e6 → SPF; GCD/LCM mixed with construction, games, or range queries.
hints.3: Say: gcd(shifts)→diffs; pairwise-LCM gcd→second-min exponents; floor(n/i) in √n blocks; skins are k-th/reconstruct divisors, raise/share-prime gcd, trailing zeros/K|N!, and Row-GCD/Orac-LCM identities.

phases.goal: Choose the right identity rewrite—floor blocks, GCD-of-diffs, second-min exponents, SPF pairwise check, or Legendre/Ω—before coding.

must_hit.point: Floor blocks: ⌊n/i⌋ is constant on [i, n/⌊n/i⌋]; jump the right endpoint (Everyone is a Winner / CSES Sum of Divisors).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the constant segment [i, n/⌊n/i⌋] and jumping the right endpoint.

must_hit.point: GCD of shifts: gcd(a+x,b+x)=gcd(a−b,b+x); Row GCD reduces an n×m family to one gcd of pairwise diffs plus each bⱼ.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the gcd(a+x,b+x)=gcd(a−b,b+x) identity and precomputing gcd of diffs.

must_hit.point: GCD of pairwise LCMs: per prime keep the two smallest exponents; answer uses the second-min (Orac and LCM)—not “min of all”, and not Orac and Models.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Keeps two smallest exponents and takes second-min; rejects plain min-of-all and Orac-and-Models confusion.

must_hit.point: SPF pairwise vs setwise: pairwise-coprime iff each prime appears in ≤1 element; setwise iff global gcd=1 (ABC177E / Bash's Big Day).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates pairwise (each prime ≤1 element) from setwise (global gcd=1).

must_hit.point: Trailing zeros / K|N!: only primes 2 and 5 matter for roundness—balance min(v₂,v₅) under multiply-budget (Make It Round); factorial multiples use Legendre counts + binary search on N (ABC280D).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Balances 2/5 under budget m, or factors K and binary-searches N with Legendre counts.

probes: How do you rewrite floor sums or gcd(aᵢ+x) / gcd of pairwise LCMs before coding?
When do you use SPF pairwise checks versus Legendre/2×5 trailing-zero balance?

hints.1: Look for a floor-segment jump, a shift→diff identity, or a per-prime exponent rule before brute force.
hints.2: Floor → [i, n/⌊n/i⌋]; Row GCD → gcd of diffs; Orac LCM → second-min exponents; SPF → each prime ≤1 element; zeros → 2 and 5 / Legendre.
hints.3: Say: jump floor blocks; gcd(a+x,b+x)=gcd(a−b,b+x); second-min exponents not min-of-all; pairwise ≠ setwise; balance min(v₂,v₅) or BS N with Legendre.

phases.goal: Show O(√n) divisor listing, SPF factoring, floor-block loops, and the concrete constructions interviewers ask to sketch.

must_hit.point: k-th divisor / Almost All Divisors: collect both i and n/i, sort, pick k-th; candidate n=min·max then verify the sorted proper-divisor list matches.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Collects i and n/i (or states n=min·max plus verify), not a half-list without the pair.

must_hit.point: SPF precompute: sieve spf[x] up to max Aᵢ, then factor each value in O(log A); count frequency per prime for “share a factor” (Bash's Big Day).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sieves SPF to max Aᵢ and factors in O(log A), then buckets by prime.

must_hit.point: Floor-block sum/list: rewrite ∑σ(i) as ∑ᵢ i·⌊n/i⌋ and advance i to the end of each constant ⌊n/i⌋ segment in O(√n).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes the i·⌊n/i⌋ rewrite and jumps i to the segment end.

must_hit.point: Exponent vectors mod k (Power Products): map each a to its prime-exponent vector mod k; pair with the complementary vector so the product is a perfect k-th power (every exponent ≡0 mod k).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Hashes residue vectors and looks up the complement for a perfect k-th power.

must_hit.point: GCD on ranges of diffs (Integers Have Friends): a subarray shares a common divisor >1 iff gcd of consecutive |diffs|>1; sparse table / stack on those diffs while gcd stays >1.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Builds RMQ/sparse-table (or stack) over consecutive diffs and expands while gcd>1.

probes: Walk through listing the k-th divisor or reconstructing n from almost-all divisors.
How do you implement SPF factoring, a floor-block sum, or complementary exponent vectors mod k?

hints.1: Start from collecting paired divisors or sieving SPF before any fancy DS.
hints.2: k-th → i and n/i then sort; reconstruct → min·max + verify; floor → jump segment ends; Power Products → residue vector + complement.
hints.3: Say: collect i and n/i; n=min·max then verify; spf up to max Aᵢ then O(log A) factor; ∑ i·⌊n/i⌋ with right-endpoint jumps; hash exponent vectors mod k and look up complements; sparse-table gcd of diffs.

phases.goal: Match the feasible bound—O(√n) floor/divisors, SPF O(log A) per factor, or n·√A / A log A—to the constraint.

must_hit.point: Distinct ⌊n/i⌋ values and divisor-sum rewrites run in O(√n) floor blocks—required when n≤1e12 (CSES Sum of Divisors); never loop i=1..n.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States O(√n) floor blocks and rejects a 1..n loop for n≤1e12.

must_hit.point: With values ≤1e6, SPF sieve once then factor in O(log A) beats per-query O(√n) factorization across many aᵢ.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites ≤1e6 SPF precompute and O(log A) per factor versus repeated √n peels.

must_hit.point: Depth-pass NT is in play when the intended bound is n·√A or A log A feasible (harmonic sieves on frequencies, Enlarge GCD-style multiples counts).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names n·√A or A log A (or harmonic multiples on frequencies) as the feasible regime.

probes: For n≤1e12 floor sums, what complexity is acceptable and what loop is forbidden?
When Aᵢ are ≤1e6, why prefer SPF over per-query √n factorization?

hints.1: Match the loop shape to n versus max Aᵢ.
hints.2: Large single n → O(√n) floor blocks; many bounded Aᵢ → SPF + O(log A); array+divisor frequency work → n·√A / A log A.
hints.3: Say: O(√n) floor blocks for n≤1e12 (never i=1..n); SPF to ≤1e6 then O(log A) factors; harmonic/Enlarge-GCD style fits n·√A or A log A.

phases.goal: Catch second-min vs min, pairwise vs setwise, a=1 edges, and the n=1e12 floor-loop trap.

must_hit.point: Orac and LCM: answer exponent is the second-minimum among aᵢ (min if unique)—using “min of all” is wrong; also not the same problem as Orac and Models.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Corrects min-of-all to second-min and separates Orac and Models.

must_hit.point: Never loop i=1..n for floor(n/i) work when n=1e12 (Everyone is a Winner / CSES Sum of Divisors)—jump each constant segment’s right endpoint.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects the 1..n loop and states segment-end jumps for n=1e12.

must_hit.point: Plus and Multiply: reverse by /a while divisible else −b, but handle the a=1 edge carefully.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls out the a=1 edge in the peel/subtract loop.

must_hit.point: ABC177E: pairwise-coprime is “each prime hits ≤1 element,” not the same as setwise coprime (global gcd=1).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States both tests and refuses collapsing them into one gcd check.

must_hit.point: Almost All Divisors: candidate n=min·max is not enough—must verify the sorted proper-divisor list matches.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Requires the verify step after n=min·max.

probes: What goes wrong if you take the minimum exponent instead of the second-minimum for gcd of pairwise LCMs?
Which traps show up on n=1e12 floor loops, a=1 in Plus and Multiply, or pairwise vs setwise coprime?

hints.1: Check exponent rule, floor-loop shape, a=1, and pairwise vs setwise wording.
hints.2: Orac LCM → second-min not min; n=1e12 → jump segments; Plus and Multiply → a=1; ABC177E → each prime ≤1 vs global gcd=1.
hints.3: Also: Orac and LCM ≠ Orac and Models; Almost All Divisors needs verify after n=min·max.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: ⌊n/i⌋ is constant on [i, n/⌊n/i⌋]; jump the right endpoint in O(√n). Never loop i=1..n for n=1e12 (Everyone is a Winner / CSES Sum of Divisors).

tradeoffs.topic: GCD identity rewrite vs brute force over shifts or pairwise LCMs
tradeoffs.strong_answer: gcd(a+x,b+x)=gcd(a−b,b+x) reduces Row GCD to gcd of diffs plus each bⱼ; gcd of pairwise LCMs collapses per prime to the second-min exponent—interviewers prefer the one-line rewrite over brute force.

tradeoffs.topic: Second-min exponents vs min of all (Orac and LCM)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Per prime keep the two smallest exponents across the array; the answer uses the second-min (min if unique)—not “min of all”, and not Orac and Models.

tradeoffs.topic: Pairwise-coprime SPF check vs setwise gcd=1
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Pairwise iff each prime appears in ≤1 element; setwise iff global gcd=1 (ABC177E)—different predicates.

tradeoffs.topic: SPF O(log A) factoring vs per-query O(√n) when values ≤1e6
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Sieve spf[x] up to max Aᵢ and factor in O(log A); that regime is what ≤1e6 invites, versus repeated √n peels.

tradeoffs.topic: Trailing-zero 2×5 balance vs full factorization for K|N!
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Roundness only cares about primes 2 and 5—balance min(v₂,v₅) under multiply-budget m (Make It Round); smallest N with K|N! factors K and binary-searches N with Legendre counts (ABC280D).

gotchas.trap: Using the minimum exponent across the array for gcd of pairwise LCMs.
gotchas.correction: Per prime, keep the two smallest exponents; answer exponent is the second-minimum (min if unique)—Orac and LCM, not “min of all”.

gotchas.trap: Treating Orac and LCM like Orac and Models.
gotchas.correction: They are different problems; Orac and LCM is the second-min-exponent rewrite for gcd of pairwise LCMs.

gotchas.trap: Looping i=1..n for distinct ⌊n/i⌋ or ∑ i·⌊n/i⌋ when n=1e12.
gotchas.correction: Jump i to the end of each constant ⌊n/i⌋ segment; the work is O(√n).

gotchas.trap: Ignoring a=1 in Plus and Multiply’s reverse /a or −b walk.
gotchas.correction: While n divisible by a, peel; else subtract b—handle a=1 carefully.
Pairwise: each prime hits ≤1 element (SPF); setwise: global gcd=1 (ABC177E).

gotchas.trap: Taking n=min·max from a divisor list without verification.
gotchas.correction: Almost All Divisors: candidate n=min·max, then verify the sorted proper-divisor list matches.

gotchas.trap: Forgetting that trailing zeros / roundness only involve primes 2 and 5.
gotchas.correction: Balance min(v₂,v₅) under the multiply-budget m (Make It Round); same Legendre idea as ABC280D factorial multiples.
